title: State of Maharashtra vs Mohd. Yakub
summary: The accused induced the complainant to invest money in a fake import business. The court held that dishonest intention existed from the beginning, constituting cheating under Section 420 IPC.

title: Ramesh Kumar vs State of Punjab
summary: The accused misappropriated entrusted funds for personal use. The court convicted under Section 406 IPC.

title: Anil Mahajan vs Bhor Industries Ltd.
summary: The court distinguished between breach of contract and cheating, stating that mere failure to fulfill promise does not constitute cheating unless fraudulent intent existed initially.

title: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma vs State of Bihar
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that dishonest intention at the time of making the promise is essential to constitute cheating.

title: S.W. Palanitkar vs State of Bihar
summary: Directors were accused of siphoning funds. The court examined criminal liability in contractual relationships.

title: Dalip Kaur vs Jagnar Singh
summary: Court held that civil disputes should not be converted into criminal cases unless clear fraudulent intention is proven.

title: Kishan Singh vs Gurpal Singh
summary: Sale deed was forged to deceive buyer. Accused convicted for forgery and cheating.

title: Indian Oil Corporation vs NEPC India Ltd.
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that criminal proceedings can coexist with civil remedies in cases of fraudulent conduct.

title: Vesa Holdings vs State of Kerala
summary: The court emphasized distinction between dishonest inducement and breach of promise.

title: Alpic Finance Ltd vs P. Sadasivan
summary: Court ruled that deception for financial gain constitutes cheating.

title: K.C. Builders vs ACIT
summary: False statements and suppression of facts amounted to fraud against revenue authorities.

title: Medchl Chemicals vs Biological E Ltd.
summary: Court ruled compensation must be proportional to actual damage suffered due to breach.

title: Rashmi Kumar vs Mahesh Kumar
summary: Husband misappropriated wife's property; convicted under criminal breach of trust.

title: Devender Kumar vs State of Haryana
summary: Electronic records admitted under Section 65B of Evidence Act.

title: Bhim Singh vs State of J&K
summary: Court awarded compensation for illegal detention under inherent powers.

title: Kishore Samrite vs State of UP
summary: Court imposed penalties for misuse of judicial process.

title: State of UP vs Deoman Upadhyaya
summary: Court ruled that confession must be voluntary to be admissible.

title: Gopal Das vs State of Assam
summary: All accused held liable for joint criminal act.

title: State of Tamil Nadu vs Nalini
summary: Court elaborated liability under criminal conspiracy law.

title: P. Chidambaram vs Directorate of Enforcement
summary: Court discussed arrest without warrant under cognizable offence rules.
